gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-010 directly identifies that L-chain supports can leave the current refinement domain, violate nestedness, and require upward parent-domain closure.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Adding supports for problematic-pair repair without enforcing containment or propagating the required parent closure can violate the nested hierarchical-domain invariant and invalidate exactness.

component_coverage.gold_component: L-chain support insertion can violate nested refinement-domain containment and requires recursive parent closure.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives an explicit support-outside-domain example, identifies the resulting violation of nestedness, and proposes fine-to-coarse parent-domain closure.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold bundles two independently diagnosable candidate-state defects: the missing unchecked-function state and incomplete maintenance of all newly possible pairs. ISSUE-008 diagnoses the first, while ISSUE-009 independently diagnoses failure to enqueue newly introduced candidate functions and pairs.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The candidate-function and candidate-pair state is not maintained completely: the printed procedure lacks the required unresolved-function state, and updates can omit pairs involving newly introduced functions, so termination does not certify that all problematic pairs were checked.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern is left unrecognised; ISSUE-008 covers the undefined state and ISSUE-009 covers incomplete candidate discovery, using a different manifestation of the same candidate-completeness obligation.
gold_decisions.combination_explanation: The gold entry contains distinct defects: an interface/state omission in which unchecked_funcs is not returned or initialized, and a separate completeness defect in which newly introduced functions are not all added to the candidate-pair set. ISSUE-008 gives a self-contained diagnosis of the missing state; ISSUE-009 gives a self-contained diagnosis of omitted newly contained functions and pairs. Together they cover the full gold concern.

component_coverage.gold_component: The main procedure uses unchecked_funcs without receiving or initializing it, leaving the candidate state undefined.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-008 explicitly identifies the missing returned/initialized unchecked-function state and proposes returning and assigning it with the pairs.

component_coverage.gold_component: Even a naive initialization with only new corners would omit pairs between newly introduced functions and existing unresolved functions, so termination would not certify complete checking.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-009 independently shows that chain repair can introduce splines not already queued and that omitted pairs can leave problematic intersections undetected; it prescribes recomputing and enqueueing all newly contained splines and pairs.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-007 directly identifies that level-L marks are never processed to create level L+1 and proposes processing the former finest level consistently.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The refinement loop excludes the current finest level, so permitted level-L marks are not refined and newly created finest-level conditions are not checked.

component_coverage.gold_component: Marked elements at the current finest level are skipped, preventing creation of level L+1.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction states the exact loop-boundary failure, its L=0 consequence, and the required level-(L+1) processing repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-012 directly identifies deletion of pre-existing problematic pairs when both supports avoid the new marks and the resulting failure for arbitrary input hierarchies.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Filtering out old problematic pairs unrelated to the current marks silently ignores defects already present in the input, so the no-problematic-intersections postcondition is not unconditional.

component_coverage.gold_component: Initializer deletion of pre-existing pairs disjoint from current marks can leave those pairs in the output.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction supplies the same deletion mechanism, arbitrary-input countercase, violated postcondition, and full-validation repair.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-011 directly identifies that arbitrary element marks are not complete zero-form support unions and can violate the refinement-domain hypothesis, with a support-closure repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Directly adding arbitrary marked elements does not ensure that the updated refinement domain is a union of the required level-ell zero-form supports, undermining the hierarchical-space and exactness assumptions.

component_coverage.gold_component: Marked elements may be strictly smaller than covering zero-form supports, so direct domain union can leave the admissible hierarchical-domain class.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies arbitrary marked cells as failing the complete-support-union hypothesis, explains the resulting exactness failure, and prescribes enlarging marks to support closure.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 explicitly identifies the endpoint-vanishing boundary-space definition, the nonzero tangential trace of the test field, and the resulting invalid exact-reproduction claim.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The claimed natural-boundary test field is not in the endpoint-vanishing 1-form space, so the stated membership and exact-reproduction rationale are invalid unless unconstrained spaces are used.

component_coverage.gold_component: The endpoint-vanishing definition excludes u=(x(1-x),0), invalidating the stated space membership and exact reproduction in the first test.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction directly links the zero-trace boundary-space distinction to exclusion of the test field and prescribes unconstrained spaces for natural-boundary tests.
